offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

The ledger consumer posts events at a rate rising to about 3.3/s, with a few already_processed. It is consuming, not stalled.
All containers are running and healthy with 0 restarts. All started around 11:07:21-29.
All services were created at 11:07:21 with normal settings: idempotent ledger handler, dead_letter for bad events, cents, v1 secret.
The money check passes. All 1097 events were posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced, and the ledger and payments match the provider. It settled in 0.24s, so there is no backlog.

proposed_fix.summary: Take no action on the services. Review the alert rule: check its series and labels (the metric labels by 'consumer', not 'group') and its 'for' duration. Consider a startup grace period so a freshly started stack does not page on transient lag. If it fires again, query klaxon_kafka_consumer_lag per partition at the firing time.

diagnosis.blast_radius: None. The running system is not changed. Any edit to the alert rule only changes how sensitive alerting is.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo. Any later alert-rule change can be reverted to the current rule definition.
